data.name: Shoshanna
data.gender_notes: Shoshanna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Shoshana, meaning ‘rose’ or ‘grace’. In the Bible, Shoshanna (Shoshannah) is a variant of the name Hagar, the Egyptian concubine of Abraham. It symbolizes God's grace and favor towards Hagar and her son Ishmael. The name Shoshanna carries the meaning “Gift of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Shoshanna usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of God's love and grace
data.etymology: Shoshanna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shoshanna total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shoshanna has a rich cultural history that extends beyond its biblical roots. In various ancient cultures, roses were considered symbols of love, beauty, and passion. Naming a girl Shoshanna would signify the hope for her to embody these qualities and grow into a woman who is beautiful, gracious, and full of love.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Shoshanna holds a deep spiritual significance. It represents God's unending grace and love towards everyone, as seen in the story of Hagar and Ishmael. Shoshanna is a reminder that no matter our background or circumstances, we can all experience God's favor and blessings. Through her name, young girls named Shoshanna can be inspired to embody the grace and love of God in their own lives.
